title: Tech Jitters are Back. Bonds Like It
summary:
Tech Jitters are Back. Bonds Like It 

             
             
            As has been the case for the past several weeks, the near-term fate of the rate rally is dependent on tech jitters. While those had leveled off in a sideways pattern over the first few days of the week, they resurfaced today, both at the NYSE open and close. The 4pm move was bigger for stocks and directly linked to weak guidance in Intel and Amazon earnings releases. Bonds were already moderately stronger on the day after the 9:30am gains, but improved even more after the 4pm NYSE close.

title: Rates Dip to New Multi-Week Lows
summary: After 4 rather uneventful trading days, the bond market (which underlies interest rate movement) experienced a bit more volatility today. Fortunately, it was volatility in a friendly direction.  10yr Treasury yields ended the day at their lowest level since September 22nd. Mortgage rates dropped to their lowest mark since September 23rd for the average lender.   [thirtyyearmortgagerates]  Bond gains coincided with moments of weakness in the stock market, primarily at the 9:30am NYSE open and the 4pm close. Weaker guidance from the likes of Intel and Amazon reinforced the recently cautious narrative surrounding tech and the AI buildout, sending tech stocks sharply lower at 4pm.  NOTE: today's mortgage rate index has not yet been updated for any additional lender reprices that may hit in the coming hours.

title: Non-QM Execution, Real Estate Agent Service, UAD 3.6, Jumbo Products; Freddie Earnings
summary: Artificial intelligence continues to capture the imagination of a wide range of companies, including lenders. “Why Underwriting Is the Right Problem for AI to Solve First,” is a topic on a recent Thought Leadership piece. It will be a topic on today’s The Big Picture with James Sais, the head of mortgage lending at Fifth Third Bank. You may be thinking about rolling AI out, but who’s in charge, you or it? In its IPO filing Monday, Anthropic (ANT) warned prospective investors that artificial intelligence systems could pose catastrophic risks as they operate with greater autonomy. "Concerns have been raised both within our organization and by other researchers, regulators, policymakers, and industry participants that sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy," it said. And you want this to run your company, or manage your money? (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by FICO. As the industry's most predictive credit score, FICO Score 10T combines proven performance with deeper insight into borrower behavior to help support a stronger and more resilient housing finance system. Today’s has an interview with Sela’s Nate Becker on mortgage voice agents, their performance, adoption, and the future role of loan officers.)

title: No Whammies From PCE Data. Tech Plunge Helping
summary: PCE inflation was almost perfectly in line with even the unrounded expectations. The monthly core number was 0.32 vs 0.34 (or .3 vs .3 on most econ calendars). Perhaps the modest miss helps explain the modest drop in yields at 8:30am.  All in all though, it was a small enough response as to obviate any further consideration. Bonds experienced a much bigger move at the 9:30am NYSE open when multiple large tech companies saw their stocks plunge sharply (led by Alphabet aka Google). A few instances of new corporate bond issues have accounted for small bounces in yields (Microsoft and Verizon, specifically).

title: CrossCountry Widens VantageScore Eligibility, Reports $2,500 In Savings
summary: CrossCountry Mortgage is reporting an estimated $2,500 in average borrower savings from its adoption of VantageScore 4.0, adding to a growing body of lender-reported results showing how competition between credit scoring models is translating into lower loan costs.The Cleveland-based lender said Thursday that, during its first 60 days of implementation, loans receiving a more favorable credit score through VantageScore 4.0 saw an average reduction of 62 basis points in loan-level pricing adjustments (LLPAs).

title: I Told A Borrower His Credit Was Crap. The Real Problem Was Me.
summary: "Listen, your credit is crap. If you don't want the deal, move on."I said that to a borrower once. Word for word. The part that bothers me now isn't just what I said. It's that I didn't think about him again. He walked out, and I went right back to work.Early in my career, I worked for a guy whose philosophy was pretty simple: You're only as good as your last month. Plenty of fish in the sea. If someone didn't want the deal, NEXT. He used to tell me, "I want 100 deals a month out of your office, Enbody. I don't care if that's 10 MLOs or 100 MLOs. I want 100 deals."

title: Fed Holds Rates, But Pricing Pressures Persist
summary: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady Wednesday, but rising Treasury yields and fresh inflation data are keeping pressure on the factors that determine lender pricing, complicating rate-lock decisions and financing calculations for borrowers already stretching to qualify.The Fed voted 10-2 to maintain its benchmark federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4%, following a quarter-point increase in September. Two policymakers favored another immediate increase, underscoring concerns that inflation remains too high.

title: Another Bank Exits Mortgage Origination, Citing Lack Of Scale
summary: Enterprise Bank & Trust is exiting mortgage origination, joining several banks that have withdrawn from residential lending operations in recent years amid concerns about profitability, competition, and the cost of maintaining origination platforms.Jim Lally, CEO of parent company Enterprise Financial Services Corp., confirmed the decision during the company's Oct. 22 third-quarter earnings call, describing the move as part of a broader effort to eliminate expenses in businesses where the bank lacks sufficient scale.
